question: Which arrow stays vertical?
sources_detail: Weight W = mg acts toward the Earth's centre, so it stays vertical whatever the ramp angle.

On a ramp at angle θ, the weight splits into mg sin θ along the ramp and mg cos θ into it; with no other push perpendicular to the ramp, N = mg cos θ (OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, §6.1, 'Solving Problems with Newton's Laws').
On screen: the N arrow is drawn with length proportional to cos θ; the arc marks θ between mg and the dashed −N line, equal to the ramp angle.
caption: Tilt the ramp: which arrow stays vertical? N, F, f or mg? 👇 #physics #newtonslaws #studytok

keywords: physics, free body diagram, inclined plane, normal force, weight, Newton's laws
description: A crate on a ramp with its four forces played by characters: F (yellow) pulls up the ramp, friction f (red) holds it back, the normal force N (blue) pushes it off the ramp, the weight mg (green) hangs straight down.
As the ramp tilts from 20° to 40°, N, F and f turn with the ramp, but mg never turns: gravity always points straight down, toward the Earth's centre.
What to remember: N is perpendicular to the ramp and N = mg cos θ; the part of the weight pulling down the ramp is mg sin θ. Animation made in 3D (Blender), not filmed.
